propositions: configure_logging() sets propagate=False on the shared 'rebar' logger as process-global state that is never restored, silently breaking caplog assertions on rebar.* loggers in subsequent test phases
Tests calling configure_logging() mid-execution create a void window where caplog cannot capture rebar.* logger records emitted after the propagate mutation occurs

The test suite exhibits intermittent order-dependent failures (same tree passes on re-run without changes) because worker assignment of configure_logging()-calling tests to different processes varies across parallel test runs

Caplog assertions written positively (assert any(...), next(...)) fail visibly with StopIteration when poisoned, while negative assertions (assert not caplog.records) pass vacuously against empty capture, masking the poisoning
Removing propagate=False from configure_logging() is safe for double-logging prevention because uvicorn does not add root handlers and the marker-guarded handler is installed at most once
